name: Nuclear Threat Initiative (charityevals)
beneficiaries_note: Our build: a global catastrophe (nuclear war, a pandemic) kills people everywhere and the future lost is everyone's, so the result is spread by world population.
summary: The Nuclear Threat Initiative (Washington DC) works to cut the risk of nuclear war, nuclear terrorism and catastrophic pandemics through diplomacy and Track 2 dialogues, nuclear materials security, biosecurity policy (NTI | bio) and a small AI programme; this model covers all its programmes in 2025 ($23.3M spent). At the defaults it averts about 24 years of healthy life per $1,000, from 1 to 450 on the combined range: each dollar is valued as a typical project's cut in the forecast risks of nuclear war and pandemics (Rethink Priorities' cross-cause model, the Existential Risk Persuasion Tournament's experts), with deaths valued like every death and the future lost counted through the discount rate. The biggest uncertainty is how much a dollar of such work cuts the risk: Rethink calls its figures placeholders and the range runs ten times either way; the result also moves with the years a cut counts and the discount rate. Every branch is discounted for missing data: no outcome of the work on the risk is measured.

sections.title: Other outcomes, in this model's unit
sections.explainer: charityevals' standard step for outcomes in more than one unit (docs/normalization.md 2.6): each outcome is counted in its own unit (units of value for income and deaths, WELLBYs for life satisfaction, tonnes of CO₂e, chicken pain days) and put into this model's unit by its unit's conversion over this unit's, which the headline's conversion cancels. So each moves only with its own sliders, exactly as in a model of its own unit. The rows are fixed; don't edit them.

How far the typical project's effect applies to this charity's work
rows.explainer: How far Rethink Priorities' typical small project applies to NTI's work. Above a typical project for its diplomacy and materials work: senior access (Nunn and Moniz leading fail-safe delegations to Beijing and India in 2025, Track 2 dialogues with China's SIIS and CACDA), a record of governments adopting its products (the IAEA LEU Bank it seeded, IBBIS's Common Mechanism for DNA synthesis screening); below for public education (communications is about 38% of the nuclear spending), whose path to the risk is longest. Net 0.8, our judgment, 0.3 to 1.2.

rows.label: Share of the work no one else would have done now
rows.explainer: The share of the work no one else would have done now: other groups run nuclear Track 2 dialogues and studies (Carnegie Endowment, Belfer Center, the European and Asia Pacific Leadership Networks, which NTI also funds) and biosecurity policy work (Johns Hopkins Center for Health Security, CEPI on funders), but few combine NTI's former officials' access with its own programmes. Our judgment, 0.7 (0.4 to 0.9); that the work would have come years later is in years_of_impact.

rows.label: This charity's share of the resources behind the outcome
rows.explainer: NTI's share of the resources behind its projects: much is joint (the Deterrence Study Group and fail-safe reviews with governments' officials, the Bio Funders Compact with CEPI, partners' own staff time), the rest NTI's own. Our judgment, 0.85 (0.6 to 1).

rows.label: Share of credit used
rows.explainer: The charity's share of the resources behind the outcome; it applies whichever way credit is shared.

rows.label: Leverage and funging
rows.explainer: Whether large funders (Coefficient Giving's biosecurity grants, $7.8M over three years from 2023) would give less if small donors gave more is the room factor of @next_dollar.nuclear_threat_initiative (docs/normalization.md 2.10), so it isn't asked again here (one question per adjustment): 1, our judgment, as for every catastrophic-risk model; 0.85 to 1.05 for funging the room factor misses.

rows.label: Counted less where the outcome isn't measured for this charity
rows.explainer: Thin: no outcome of NTI's work on the risk is measured; the cut per dollar is a typical project's from Rethink Priorities' model and the chances are forecasts, so the shared missing-data step applies (docs/normalization.md 2.12).

rows.label: All adjustments combined
rows.explainer: The product of the adjustments above.

rows.label: Benefits not modelled, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: Good beyond the catastrophes counted: materials security (Materials Risk Minimization, about 19% of the area spending) also lowers the chance of a terrorist detonation, which kills far fewer than 10% of people and has no shared forecast (nuclear_smaller_per_year 0); biosafety guidance also lowers ordinary laboratory accidents. 10% (0 to 30%) of the modelled value, our judgment.

rows.label: Harm: speeding up dangerous capabilities, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: A typical project's chance of backfiring is already in the shared cut per dollar (Rethink Priorities' backfire step). NTI's work is no riskier than that: nuclear diplomacy and materials security can't advance what they guard against, and its AIxBio and biosecurity work writes guardrails rather than tools. 0, down to −5% for AI-biodesign guidance that also maps capabilities. Our judgment.

rows.label: Harm: information hazards and attention, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: Beyond a typical project's backfire (in the shared cut): published threat analyses and tabletop exercises (the Munich bioweapons exercise and its report) can show a path to a weapon, but NTI publishes guidance without technical detail. 0, down to −5%, our judgment.
